03 / Visual reference

Original Android UI & screen gallery

Nine original mobile UI screens for a premium-feeling Pomodoro + everyday Timer app. Explore themes, see interactive timer controls, and export screenshots in the bundled assets folder.

Research snapshot · November 9, 2026Android-first · Kotlin + ComposeWorking title — brand not cleared
Design direction: Celestial calm, not a literal Forest clone. The interface uses precise timer typography, restrained gradients, midnight and paper themes, original geometric stars, large actions and very short paths. These are original HTML/CSS screen mockups—not screenshots of a working Android APK. Exported PNGs ship in the ZIP as visual references.

Try the theme buttons, then start or pause the active timer demo. The screen gallery is a visual prototype; Android implementation and accessibility must follow the engineering contract.

Type scale52sp timer / 22sp header / 14sp actionSameDynamic Type adaptation; min 48dp targets

Screen layout contract

Device adaptations

  • Base design reference: ~393×852 dp Android device; mockup uses 300×606 visual scaling.
  • Small screen: collapse cards, avoid content clipping and keep full-width start.
  • Tablet: use centered timer pane with secondary tasks/history pane.
  • Landscape: horizontal arrangement for orb plus controls; no forced portrait unless justified.
  • Foldables: respond to window size classes and hinge area.

Motion & haptics

  • Progress arc should change based on remaining / total, not a free-running animation tied to elapsed time.
  • 400ms gentle transitions when enabled; disable all nonessential motion in Reduce Motion.
  • Haptic on start and completion only if user enabled; never vibrate repeatedly during focus.
  • Use vector drawable or Compose Canvas for the orbit; do not ship huge raster assets.
  • Screen reader announces remaining time meaningfully; avoid spamming announcements every second.

UX acceptance checklist

  • Focus and Timer selectable from the first screen; timer start is obvious without onboarding.
  • All controls available with TalkBack, keyboard, and large font sizes.
  • Bottom navigation does not cover timer action on 360dp-wide devices.
  • When stage completes, show “Break ready” with Start now / Later / Skip instead of assuming auto-start.
  • Provide honest notification-permission and precision fallback messaging.
  • Support dark, light, and reduced motion; colors never carry all meaning.
  • Paywall is optional and dismissible; no countdown countdowns, deceptive trial phrasing or fake limited-time deals.
The PNG exports show the original prototypes (not competitor images). Use the layout logic and token definitions to implement native Compose components; do not use the HTML screenshots as background images inside the Android app.
